sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed by anti-FLAG flow cytometry on non-permeabilized cells in two independent studies (PMC7769003, PMC8550936). FLAG-tagged WT LDLRAD3 supported VEEV pseudovirus infection in Neuro2a cells, demonstrating preserved receptor function.
sites.rationale: All four ledger lines describe the identical junction: an N-terminal FLAG tag placed immediately downstream of the signal peptide in full-length, membrane-anchored LDLRAD3. The signal peptide spans residues 1–17 (authoritative landmark), so the tag sits between residue 17 (S) and residue 18 (Q), the mature N-terminus. No paper names a residue number explicitly, but exactly one extracellular terminus exists (the mature N-terminus at 18), making the junction uniquely determined by topology. Python verification confirms residue 17 = S and residue 18 = Q in the canonical 345-aa sequence. Full-length mouse/human LDLRAD3 cDNA bearing an N-terminal FLAG tag inserted downstream of the signal sequence (residues 1–17) was expressed in ΔB4galt7 ΔLdlrad3 Neuro2a cells via lentiviral transduction. Surface expression was confirmed by anti-FLAG flow cytometry on non-permeabilized cells (L1, PMC7769003) and by plasma-membrane staining in a second independent study (L2–L4, PMC8550936). The same FLAG-tagged WT construct was used as the positive control in SINV–VEEV(TrD)–GFP infection assays (L3).

sources.claim: Anti-FLAG staining of Δ B4galt7 N2a cells (control, black) and lentivirus complemented Δ B4galt7 Δ Ldlrad3 N2a cells with empty vector (red) or Ldlrad3 cDNA (blue) containing an N-terminal FLAG-tag sequence ( left panel ).

literature_notes: Ledger lines L1–L4 all converge on a single site: the N-terminal FLAG tag inserted after the signal peptide cleavage site (after residue 17, before the mature N-terminus at residue 18). L1 (PMC7769003) and L2–L4 (PMC8550936) are independent publications, both confirming surface display by anti-FLAG flow cytometry on non-permeabilized cells; L3 additionally shows the FLAG-tagged construct supports VEEV infection, establishing functional integrity. No ledger line describes any internal extracellular loop insertion, any C-terminal extracellular tag (the C-terminus is intracellular), or any intracellular insertion. The intracellular C-terminal tail (residues 195–345) is not proposed because no ledger line supports a surface tag there. No other sites were found.
